newsitem.title: UK: ATHLETICS-BROWN EDGES OUT KOMEN IN CROSS-COUNTRY CHALLENGE.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-BROWN EDGES OUT KOMEN IN CROSS-COUNTRY CHALLENGE.

text.p: Britain's Jon Brown continued his good run of form by winning the 9.3 km second round of the IAAF World Cross Challenge series on Saturday.

Brown clocked 28 minutes 24 seconds after pulling away from Kenya's Daniel Komen in the final kilometre. The pair had duelled throughout the final part of the race after leaving the rest of the field behind. Komen, world 3,000 metres record holder, finished three seconds behind.
In the last month Brown has beaten Kenya's Paul Tergat, reigning world cross-country champion, in a race in Spain and also won the European cross-country title in Charleroi, Belgium.
Ethopia's Geta Wami, women's world cross-country champion, won the women's 5.2 km race in 17:32.
Wami sprinted clear of Romania's Elena Fidatof and Britain's Paula Radcliffe 150 metres from the line to bounce back after finishing only third in the opening race in Brussels last Sunday.
Fidatof was second in 17:33 with Radcliffe third in 17:38.
